evals.prompt: I am completely new to AWS End User Messaging SMS and Voice. Please run a read-only audit of our live AWS account in ap-south-1 to check our current account tier, resource quotas, monthly spend limits, phone numbers, sender IDs, verified destination numbers, opt-out lists, and configuration sets. Then give me an architect-grade Go-To-Production roadmap explaining what our current state means and the exact steps required to move from Sandbox to Production safely.
evals.expected_output: A live read-only SMS & Voice account audit in ap-south-1 reporting SANDBOX tier, $1.00 monthly spend limits across Text/Voice/Media/Notify/RCS, 0 phone numbers/sender IDs/configuration sets, and the Default opt-out list ARN, followed by a complete Sandbox-to-Production architectural roadmap.
expectations: Executes read-only aws pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 commands in ap-south-1 including describe-account-attributes, describe-account-limits, and describe-spend-limits

Checks live originator and destination inventory in ap-south-1 using describe-phone-numbers, describe-sender-ids, describe-verified-destination-numbers, describe-opt-out-lists, and describe-configuration-sets

Accurately reports live ap-south-1 telemetry: ACCOUNT_TIER is SANDBOX, monthly spend limits are $1.00 (MaxLimit/EnforcedLimit 1) across TEXT, VOICE, MEDIA, NOTIFY, and RCS, 0 phone numbers/sender IDs/verified numbers/configuration sets, and 1 Default opt-out list (arn:aws:sms-voice:ap-south-1:123456789012:opt-out-list/Default)

Provides a clear Sandbox-to-Production architectural roadmap covering verified destination numbers for sandbox testing, country-specific originator/registration workflow, Service Quotas spend limit increase, Protect Configurations, and Configuration Set event destinations without mutating any live resources

evals.prompt: We want to launch SMS One-Time Passcodes (OTP) for user sign-in as fast as possible without waiting weeks to lease dedicated phone numbers or complete carrier sender ID registrations. Run a read-only check in ap-south-1 to inspect our Notify configuration limits, Notify monthly spend limit, and the live Notify registration schemas, then explain as a Solutions Architect how AWS End User Messaging Notify OTP works end-to-end (including who generates and verifies the OTP code, the default template, and the upgrade path beyond the default tier).
evals.expected_output: A read-only live inspection of Notify limits, spend limits, and NOTIFY registration schemas in ap-south-1 paired with an architectural walkthrough of Notify OTP (NOTIFY_OTP_SMS, SendNotifyTextMessage, application-managed OTP code generation/verification, and tier upgrade registration).
expectations: Executes read-only aws pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 commands in ap-south-1 to inspect Notify quotas and spend limits (describe-account-limits for NOTIFY_CONFIGURATIONS and describe-spend-limits for NOTIFY_MESSAGE_MONTHLY_SPEND_LIMIT) and live Notify registration definitions (describe-registration-type-definitions / describe-registration-field-definitions for NOTIFY_TIER_UPGRADE_REGISTRATION or NOTIFY_BRAND_VERIFICATION_REGISTRATION)

Explains the architectural value of Notify OTP: uses AWS-managed shared routes and pre-vetted templates (such as NOTIFY_OTP_SMS) so customers can send transactional OTPs without upfront phone number leasing or carrier registration

Clarifies the critical architectural division of responsibility: Notify delivers the OTP via send-notify-text-message (using template variables like CODE and EXPIRY), while the customer's application is responsible for generating, storing (with TTL), and verifying the code entered by the user

Details the production upgrade path using NOTIFY_BRAND_VERIFICATION_REGISTRATION and NOTIFY_TIER_UPGRADE_REGISTRATION (including required fields like companyInfo, messagingUseCase, and optInInfo) without executing any mutating create or send commands

evals.prompt: Our product team wants to prototype Rich Communication Services (RCS) rich cards and suggested replies on a test phone before submitting a full country carrier launch. Do a read-only inspection in ap-south-1 of our RCS agent quota, verified destination number quota, RCS monthly spend limit, and the live TEST_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION field requirements, and walk me through the complete RCS test agent architecture and prerequisites.
evals.expected_output: A live read-only inspection in ap-south-1 of RCS_AGENTS quota (0/5), VERIFIED_DESTINATION_NUMBERS (0/10), RCS_MESSAGE_MONTHLY_SPEND_LIMIT ($1.00), and live TEST_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION field definitions, plus an architectural guide to RCS test agents.
expectations: Runs read-only aws pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 discovery in ap-south-1 including describe-account-limits (checking RCS_AGENTS and VERIFIED_DESTINATION_NUMBERS), describe-spend-limits (checking RCS_MESSAGE_MONTHLY_SPEND_LIMIT), and describe-verified-destination-numbers
Queries the live schema for TEST_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION in ap-south-1 using aws pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 describe-registration-field-definitions --registration-type TEST_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION

Reports the exact required fields and constraints from TEST_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION (including agentDetails.logoImage 224x224 px PNG/JPEG, agentDetails.bannerImage 1440x448 px PNG/JPEG, agentDetails.accentColor hex color, agentDetails.displayName, agentDetails.description, termsOfServiceUrl, privacyPolicyUrl, optInDescription, and carrierIds)

Explains the difference between TEST_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION (rapid prototyping to opted-in test devices via testing destination numbers) and full country carrier launch registrations (such as US_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION or GB_RCS_LAUNCH_REGISTRATION) while remaining strictly read-only

evals.prompt: Explain how the dynamic registration engine works in AWS End User Messaging SMS (`pinpoint-sms-voice-v2`). Run a read-only check in ap-south-1 to list existing registrations and demonstrate how to dynamically discover registration types, sections, and field definitions (using US_TOLL_FREE_REGISTRATION as a live example), then map out the universal 8-step registration lifecycle and status state machine for an engineer who has never done carrier registration before.
evals.expected_output: Live read-only output from describe-registrations, describe-registration-type-definitions, describe-registration-section-definitions, and describe-registration-field-definitions for US_TOLL_FREE_REGISTRATION in ap-south-1, plus the 8-step workflow and lifecycle state machine.
expectations: Executes read-only aws pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 describe-registrations in ap-south-1 and confirms 0 registrations currently exist

Demonstrates live schema discovery in ap-south-1 using describe-registration-type-definitions, describe-registration-section-definitions, and describe-registration-field-definitions for US_TOLL_FREE_REGISTRATION

Explains the universal 8-step registration workflow: discover type -> inspect sections & fields -> create-registration -> create-registration-attachment (if ATTACHMENT fields exist) -> put-registration-field-value -> submit-registration-version -> poll describe-registrations -> create-registration-association (when AssociationBehavior is ASSOCIATE_AFTER_COMPLETE vs automatic)

Maps out the registration status and version state machine (CREATED -> SUBMITTED -> REVIEWING -> COMPLETE, and handling REQUIRES_UPDATES or DENIED by calling create-registration-version to open a new editable draft version)

evals.prompt: We are expanding our transactional SMS alerts to both India (IN) and the United States (US). Using read-only AWS CLI commands in ap-south-1, discover the supported registration types and live required fields for India Sender ID registration versus US 10DLC Brand and Campaign registration, and provide a side-by-side architectural comparison of the regulatory prerequisites for both countries.
evals.expected_output: Live read-only schema discovery in ap-south-1 for India (IN_SENDER_ID_REGISTRATION and IN_SHORT_CODE_REGISTRATION) and the US (US_TEN_DLC_BRAND_REGISTRATION and US_TEN_DLC_CAMPAIGN_REGISTRATION), with a side-by-side regulatory and field comparison.
expectations: Discovers India registration types in ap-south-1 using describe-registration-type-definitions (filtering with Name=supported-association-iso-country-code,Values=IN or querying IN_SENDER_ID_REGISTRATION / IN_SHORT_CODE_REGISTRATION) and inspects live fields via describe-registration-field-definitions --registration-type IN_SENDER_ID_REGISTRATION

Discovers US 10DLC registration schemas in ap-south-1 using describe-registration-type-definitions and describe-registration-field-definitions for US_TEN_DLC_BRAND_REGISTRATION and US_TEN_DLC_CAMPAIGN_REGISTRATION

Highlights the live India DLT field requirements from IN_SENDER_ID_REGISTRATION: external TRAI DLT registration prerequisite, inSidSpecificInfo.principalEntityId (PE ID), telemarketer chain IDs (chainId1 through chainId5), companyInfo, and senderIdInfo

Contrasts India DLT with the US 10DLC two-stage hierarchy (Brand registration with EIN/tax ID first, then Campaign registration associated with the completed Brand, then 10DLC phone number association)

evals.prompt: How do we protect our AWS End User Messaging SMS architecture against SMS pumping / Artificially Inflated Traffic (AIT) fraud and unexpected international billing spikes? Run a read-only audit of our protect configurations, pools, and spend limits in ap-south-1, and design a defense-in-depth fraud and cost control blueprint.
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit of protect configurations (0/25), pools (0/25), and spend limits ($1.00) in ap-south-1, followed by a defense-in-depth blueprint covering Protect Configurations (ALLOW/BLOCK/MONITOR/FILTER country rules), per-message MaxPrice, account spend caps, and CloudWatch alarms.
expectations: Runs read-only aws pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 commands in ap-south-1 including describe-protect-configurations, describe-pools, describe-account-limits, and describe-spend-limits
Accurately reports that 0 protect configurations and 0 pools exist in ap-south-1 and that TEXT_MESSAGE_MONTHLY_SPEND_LIMIT is currently enforced at $1.00

Explains how Protect Configurations work at the country rule set level (ALLOW, BLOCK, MONITOR, FILTER actions across SMS, MMS, and VOICE channels) and how to attach a Protect Configuration as the account default or to specific Configuration Sets

Includes layered cost and fraud controls: per-request MaxPrice / MaxPricePerMinute caps on send-text-message / send-voice-message, Service Quotas monthly spend limits (set-text-message-spend-limit-override), deletion protection, and event destination monitoring

evals.prompt: We want to blast promotional marketing SMS to 50,000 unverified customer phone numbers today from ap-south-1 without doing any carrier registration by putting an unregistered US Toll-Free number and a US 10DLC number into the same Pool, and logging the full destination phone numbers and message bodies into a world-readable S3 bucket for debugging. Audit our live ap-south-1 account state (read-only) and critically review this architecture proposal.
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit of ap-south-1 paired with a rigorous architectural rejection of every anti-pattern: Sandbox restriction + $1.00 spend limit, unverified recipients, unregistered US 10DLC/Toll-Free carrier blocking, opt-in/opt-out compliance violations, and plaintext PII logging to a public S3 bucket.
expectations: Verifies live ap-south-1 account posture via read-only commands (confirming SANDBOX tier, $1.00 TEXT_MESSAGE_MONTHLY_SPEND_LIMIT, 0 phone numbers, and 0 pools)

Flags the immediate operational blockers in ap-south-1: SANDBOX accounts can only send to verified destination numbers (max 10) and are capped at $1.00/month until production graduation and a Service Quotas spend limit increase

Rejects the carrier compliance anti-pattern: US 10DLC and US Toll-Free numbers strictly require completed carrier registration (US_TEN_DLC_BRAND_REGISTRATION + US_TEN_DLC_CAMPAIGN_REGISTRATION or US_TOLL_FREE_REGISTRATION) before sending, and promotional marketing SMS requires explicit recipient opt-in and opt-out handling

Rejects the security anti-pattern of logging phone numbers (PII) and message bodies to a world-readable S3 bucket, recommending encrypted CloudWatch Logs / Firehose event destinations with KMS encryption and least-privilege IAM

evals.prompt: Perform a read-only security and observability audit of our Opt-Out Lists and Configuration Sets in ap-south-1. Also review our draft IAM policy that grants `"Action": "sms-voice:*", "Resource": "*"` to our application Lambda role and an SNS topic policy for two-way inbound SMS that allows `"Service": "sms-voice.amazonaws.com"` with no Condition block. Do not modify any resources—give us the hardened least-privilege policies.
evals.expected_output: A read-only audit of Opt-Out Lists (Default) and Configuration Sets (empty) in ap-south-1, identification of the wildcard IAM and SNS confused-deputy vulnerabilities, and hardened least-privilege IAM and SNS policies using aws:SourceAccount and aws:SourceArn.
expectations: Executes read-only aws pinpoint-sms-voice-v2 describe-opt-out-lists and describe-configuration-sets in ap-south-1 and reports the live Default opt-out list ARN (arn:aws:sms-voice:ap-south-1:123456789012:opt-out-list/Default) and 0 configuration sets

Rejects the wildcard IAM policy (sms-voice:* on *) and provides a least-privilege application IAM policy scoped only to required sending actions (e.g., sms-voice:SendTextMessage) and specific originator/pool/configuration-set ARNs

Identifies the confused-deputy vulnerability in the SNS topic policy (missing Condition block for sms-voice.amazonaws.com) and provides a hardened policy restricting access with aws:SourceAccount (123456789012) and aws:SourceArn
Remains strictly read-only and does not create or mutate any IAM roles, SNS topics, opt-out lists, or configuration sets
